title: Straightedge Only
blurb: No compass: a straightedge alone, and then with one circle drawn with its center. The Poncelet–Steiner theorem says that one circle is all a straightedge needs to do everything a compass can.

items.title: A Trapezoid
items.text: $PQ$ is parallel to $AB$ exactly when the line through $S$ and $X$ meets $AB$ at its midpoint $M$.

items.title: Parallel from a Midpoint
items.text:
There’s no compass in this lesson, only a straightedge. $M$ is the midpoint of $AB$. Construct the line through $P$ parallel to $AB$.

::: Hint
It’s the trapezoid from the start of the lesson, with $A$, $B$, $M$ and $P$ given and $Q$ to be found.
:::

::: Hint
$S$ can be any point on line $AP$ beyond $P$.
:::

items.title: Midpoint from a Parallel
items.text:
Line $\ell$ is parallel to $AB$. Construct the midpoint of $AB$.

::: Hint
It’s the trapezoid from the start of the lesson, with $\ell$ as line $PQ$.
:::

::: Hint
$S$ can be any point beyond $\ell$.
:::

items.title: Harmonic Conjugate
items.text:
$A$, $B$ and $C$ lie on line $\ell$. Construct the point $D$ on $\ell$, outside $AB$, with $DA : DB = CA : CB$.

::: Hint
Draw the trapezoid from the start of the lesson with $C$ as $M$, but with $PQ$ not parallel to $AB$. Line $PQ$ crosses $\ell$ at $D$.
:::

::: Hint
$S$ can be any point off $\ell$, and $X$ any point on line $SC$.
:::

items.title: One Circle
items.text:
From here on, you get one fixed circle with its center marked. Surprisingly, when paired with a straightedge, this circle can construct anything a compass can.

The ends of any two diameters are the corners of a rectangle, so they give you two pairs of parallel lines.

items.title: Parallel
items.text:
Using just one circle with the center marked, a straightedge can construct a parallel to any line. Construct the line through $P$ and parallel to $\ell$.

::: Hint
Two diameters of $\omega$ make a rectangle, so you have pairs of parallel lines.
:::

::: Hint
A segment of $\ell$ between two parallel lines has its midpoint on the line midway between them, which goes through $O$.
:::

items.title: Perpendicular
items.text:
Construct the line through $P$ perpendicular to $\ell$.

::: Hint
Make a chord of $\omega$ parallel to $\ell$.
:::

::: Hint
The line from $O$ to the midpoint of a chord is perpendicular to it.
:::

items.title: Midpoint
items.text:
Construct the midpoint of $AB$.

::: Hint
You can draw a parallel to $AB$ now.
:::

items.title: Translate
items.text:
Construct the point $Q$ that makes $ABQP$ a parallelogram.

::: Hint
Opposite sides of a parallelogram are parallel.
:::

items.title: Rotate
items.text:
Construct the two points on $\ell$ at a distance $OA$ from $O$.

::: Hint
Line $OA$ and $\ell$ cross $\omega$ at points the same distance from $O$.
:::

::: Hint
A line parallel to the chord between those points cuts the two lines at equal distances from $O$.
:::

items.title: Scale
items.text:
$A'$ is on line $OA$. Construct the point $B'$ on line $OB$ with $OB' : OB = OA' : OA$.

::: Hint
$AB$ and $A'B'$ are parallel.
:::

items.title: Copy a Length
items.text:
Construct the two points on $\ell$ at a distance $AB$ from $P$.

::: Hint
Translate $AB$ so it starts at $O$.
:::

::: Hint
Rotate it onto the line through $O$ parallel to $\ell$, then translate it to $P$.
:::

items.title: Line Meets Circle
items.text:
Circle $\kappa$ is centered at $C$ and goes through $D$, but it isn’t drawn, and can’t be. Construct the two points where line $\ell$ crosses $\kappa$.

::: Hint
Translate $\kappa$ so its center is at $O$, then scale it about $O$ onto $\omega$.
:::

::: Hint
Do the same to $\ell$, find where it meets $\omega$, then undo both moves.
:::
